sections.name: ExcelParser (part 1)
sections.title: Sheet-by-sheet reading
sections.what: Declares the Excel parser, checks the file ending, opens the workbook and goes through each sheet. It builds a header line and one labeled line per row, then keeps each sheet that has content as its own record.
sections.why: Likely reason: a sheet is the natural unit to cite in answers. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Empty header cells are dropped, so later values can line up with the wrong column name.

sections.name: ExcelParser (part 2)
sections.title: Summary log and error exit
sections.what: Logs how many sheet records were made, returns them, and logs and re-raises any error.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells the caller the result and keeps errors visible. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: A workbook with no content at all returns an empty list rather than an error.

summary: Reads Excel workbooks and turns each sheet that has data into one searchable text record.
purpose: Lets the app search spreadsheet contents and cite the sheet a result came from.
why: Likely reason: a sheet is a natural unit for citing an answer, so each sheet becomes its own record. Reason not stated.
how: The file is opened with the saved values of formulas rather than the formulas themselves. For each sheet, the first row is read as column headers. Each later row that is not completely empty is written as one labeled line that gives its row number. A sheet with any content becomes one record that carries the sheet name and size details. Errors are logged and passed back to the caller.
inputs: A path to an .xlsx, .xls or .xlsm file.
outputs: A list with one parsed record per sheet that has content. Each record carries the sheet name and metadata for total sheets, last row and last column.
risks: The .xls ending is listed as supported, but this library reads only the newer format, so old files will probably fail. Formulas with no saved result come out blank. Empty header cells are dropped, so values can drift away from their column names. The whole workbook is loaded into memory, which can be heavy for large files.
debug: If an .xls file fails, save it as .xlsx and try again. If values are blank, open the file in Excel and save it so results are stored. If columns look misaligned, check for empty header cells.
